description: Atusher is a solo team participating in NASA Space Apps 2026. I’m interested in Earth science, satellite data, and making complex information easier to understand through maps. I’m participating independently and am not seeking team members.
summary: Atusher addresses the MODIS and VIIRS harmonization challenge by unifying data from four satellites (MODIS, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, SNPP) into a single interactive map. Users can click on any flare to see its exact location, intensity, and detection count. By integrating population density and wind direction, the tool highlights populated areas at potential risk of severe health diseases associated with gas flaring, providing critical evidence for environmental and public health research.
details:
Project Overview & How it Works:
Atusher is a geospatial web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS data (MODIS and VIIRS) to track global gas flaring. The tool integrates thermal anomalies with flaring volumes (World Bank) and wind patterns (ERA5). By clicking on any flare site, users can view its exact location, intensity, and detection count.

How NASA Data is Used:
We utilize NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors to detect thermal anomalies. We harmonized these datasets to create a unified, consistent metric for flare activity, allowing for accurate comparison without sensor bias.

Creative Features & Factors Considered:

  • Custom Bounding Box: Users can input coordinates in the "Statistics" tab to isolate a specific geographic area, instantly viewing its total flaring volume, peak months, and localized data.
  • Monthly Analysis: A dynamic line chart and data table highlight the most critical periods of thermal activity.
  • Wind Direction Reversal: To accurately show where toxic pollutants actually travel and settle, we intentionally reversed the standard wind direction from "FROM" (where wind blows from) to "TO" (where the smoke goes).
  • Global Scale: We selected 5 geographically diverse countries (USA, Iraq, UK, Algeria, Nigeria) and 3 recent years (2023-2025) to demonstrate that this is a global crisis and to ensure the highest data accuracy.

Motivation, Impact, and Scientific Evidence:
The project was inspired by an unpublished research presentation regarding Basra, Iraq (Zubair district), which highlighted a noticeable increase in leukemia and respiratory diseases among residents living downwind of flaring.
This local observation is backed by a US study on the Bakken region, North Dakota (2007–2015) by Blundell & Kokoza. Their data showed that a 1% increase in gas flaring led to a 0.73% increase in respiratory hospital visits—resulting in ~11,000 extra visits. The intended impact is to protect vulnerable populations (especially children) and help health ministries realize the severity of this issue, potentially saving lives.

Tools Used:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (Leaflet.js for mapping, Chart.js for data visualization).
  • Backend/Processing: Python (Pandas, GeoPandas, Rasterio).
  • Hosting: Netlify & GitHub.

Future Scope:
Due to time constraints, an atmospheric pollution layer was not included. In the future, we plan to integrate real-time pollution layers (like PM2.5) and develop a comprehensive health risk index to help environmental and health ministries choose safer locations for communities.
